newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House rejects effort to cut B-2 aircraft.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House rejects effort to cut B-2 aircraft.

text.p: The House of Representatives on Monday agreed to authorize purchase of additional radar-evading B-2 stealth bombers over objections of the Clinton administration.

On a vote of 216-209 it rejected an amendment to the 1998 defense authorization bill which would have eliminated $331 million for advance procurement of the Northrop Grumman Corp B-2 planes once the current production of 21 planes is completed.

The House National Security Committee had included in the defense bill sufficient funds for advance procurement of nine additional B-2 planes that Secretary of Defense William Cohen said would eventually cost a total of $21 billion before 2003.
Opponents, including Republican Rep. Mark Foley of Florida, said that in a time of bugetary constraints Congress should not authorize purchase of aircraft the administration did not want.
In a letter to Committee chairman Floyd Spence, Republican of South Carolina, Cohen said the Pentagon was unanimous in its view that "the cost of further B-2 production cannot be justified."

However, supporters of the aircraft argued that advance procurement would help maintain the country's defense industrial base. And, they said that U.S. military officials privately would support the aircraft if it weren't for the cost.
